summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of type 2 diabetes, gastroparesis, chronic abdominal pain, depression, anxiety, and recurrent UTIs was admitted for nausea, vomiting, abdominal and back pain, and dysuria. She had elevated blood pressure, acute kidney injury with creatinine of 2.6, hyperglycemia, and leukocytosis. Imaging showed no renal abnormalities. Symptoms were attributed to dehydration causing acute kidney injury and a flare of chronic gastroparesis. IV fluids led to improvement in kidney function and symptoms. Her home medications, including insulin, anti-nausea, pain, and psychiatric medications, were continued. Lisinopril was held initially but restarted as renal function improved. Antibiotics were not continued due to lack of clear infection and prior resistance. She stabilized, resumed oral intake, and was discharged home with instructions to follow up for kidney function and medication management.
